create.ponder.linear_chassis_group.text_: Linear Chassis link up with every matching chassis that touches them
Move a single one, and the whole group travels along with it
A chassis of the other kind, or one lying along another axis, is not part of the group and stays behind
Each open end of a Linear Chassis can be made sticky with a Slime Ball
Using it on a face that is already sticky coats the opposite end as well
To scrape the slime off again, Sneak and Right-Click the face with an empty hand
A sticky face carries along the row of blocks lying in front of it; the plain face leaves its row behind
Scroll on it while holding a Wrench to set exactly how far the chassis reaches
Keep CTRL held while scrolling to change the range of every connected chassis at once
Blocks on any of the other sides only come along once they are joined with Super Glue
Combining these tools, structures of nearly any shape can be moved as one Contraption
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_1: Radial Chassis join up with matching chassis stacked in a line
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_2: Turn one of them and the others follow
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_3: The four side faces of a Radial Chassis can be coated with slime
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_4: Using it on a sticky face again coats all the remaining sides
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_5: Sneak and Right-Click a face with an empty hand to take its slime off
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_6: When a block rests against a sticky face...
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_7: ...every block it can reach on the same layer, within the radius, is attached as well
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_8: Scroll on the chassis with a Wrench to choose the exact radius
create.ponder.radial_chassis.text_9: Blocks that no sticky face can reach are left where they are
create.ponder.super_glue.text_1: Super Glue binds separate blocks together so that they move as one contraption
create.ponder.super_glue.text_2: Right-Click two corner blocks one after the other to glue the box between them
create.ponder.super_glue.text_3: Hitting a glued box while holding the glue removes it again
create.ponder.super_glue.text_4: Neighbouring blocks inside the same glued box drag one another along
create.ponder.super_glue.text_5: Boxes that overlap are joined, so all of their blocks travel together
create.ponder.super_glue.text_6: Blocks that hang on or stand on others, like this torch, rarely need any glue
create.ponder.sticker.text_1: A Sticker grabs or lets go of a block whenever redstone tells it to
create.ponder.sticker.text_2: Every signal it receives flips it between holding and releasing
create.ponder.sticker.text_3: Moved as part of a contraption now, it takes the block along
create.ponder.sticker.text_4: After a second toggle the block is released and stays put
create.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_1: A Mechanical Piston shoves the blocks in front of it
create.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_2: How fast and which way it moves comes from the rotation fed into it; a plain piston leaves the blocks behind when it retracts
create.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_3: A Sticky Mechanical Piston also pulls the blocks it touches back with it
create.ponder.piston_pole.text_1: With no Extension Poles at its back, a Mechanical Piston will not budge
create.ponder.piston_pole.text_2: The number of poles attached behind it sets how far it can extend
create.ponder.mechanical_piston_modes.he: Movement Modes of the Mechanical Piston
create.ponder.mechanical_piston_modes.te: Once the piston comes to a halt, the structure it carried is placed back as ordinary blocks
Its value panel lets you keep the structure moving as an entity forever, or only place it when it returns to where it started
create.ponder.rope_pulley.text_1: Rope Pulleys lift and lower the blocks beneath them once they are given Rotational Force
create.ponder.rope_pulley.text_2: Which way they go, and how fast, depends on the rotation they receive
create.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.header: Movement Modes of the Rope Pulley
create.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.text_1: When the pulley stops, the structure it lowered is turned back into placed blocks
create.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.text_2: With its value panel it can be told to never place the blocks, or to place them only back at the starting point
create.ponder.rope_pulley_multi_rope.tex: When one pulley turns the blocks below it into a contraption...
...any other pulley on the same layer above it hooks onto the structure too
Those extra pulleys need no power of their own: their ropes are only for show
create.ponder.rope_pulley_attachment.hea: Moving Pulleys as part of a Contraption
create.ponder.rope_pulley_attachment.tex: When a pulley is itself carried along by another contraption...
...whatever hangs from it is dragged along as well
Keep in mind that a pulley can only be moved while it is not running
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_1: Elevator Pulleys carry a structure up and down between floors that you mark
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_2: First, build the cabin you want to move
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_3: Then place two Redstone Contacts so that they face each other...
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_4: ...and glue the inner one to the cabin
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_5: Adding Contraption Controls makes it easy to pick a floor from inside
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_6: Make sure the pulley is supplied with Rotational Force
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_7: Right-Click the pulley to assemble the elevator
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_8: The contact that stayed behind has become an Elevator Contact
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_9: Every Elevator Contact stands for one floor, and its settings can be edited
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_10: Other Redstone Contacts placed in the same column are converted as well
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_11: A redstone pulse sent into a contact calls the cabin to that floor
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_12: Its travel speed depends on how fast the pulley is turning
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_13: Riding inside, scroll on the controls to pick a floor, then click to go there
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_14: Right-Click the pulley again to turn the cabin back into blocks
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_15: Sliding doors on the cabin open and close on their own
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_16: While the cabin is at its floor, an Elevator Contact gives off a redstone signal
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_17: Handy for opening doors or setting off effects when it arrives
create.ponder.elevator_pulley.text_18: A Display Link placed on any contact can show which floor the elevator is on
create.ponder.elevator_pulley_multi_rope: As soon as one pulley assembles its contraption...
...the other pulleys sharing its layer link up with the same structure
They don't need to be powered; the extra ropes are purely decorative
create.ponder.windmill_source.header: Generating Rotational Force using Windmill Bearings
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_1: A Windmill Bearing holds on to the block right in front of it
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_2: Use Super Glue to turn the blocks around it into one movable structure
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_3: With enough sail-like blocks in it, that structure can work as a windmill
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_4: Right-Click the bearing to set it spinning: it now supplies Rotational Force
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_5: The more sail blocks it has, the faster it turns
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_6: Its value panel sets which way it rotates
create.ponder.windmill_source.text_7: Right-Click it again at any time to stop it and rebuild the structure
create.ponder.windmill_structure.text_1: Any structure will do as a windmill, provided it holds at least 8 sail-like blocks, such as wool
create.ponder.sail.text_1: Sails are a convenient way to build windmills
create.ponder.sail.text_2: They stick to blocks and to each other by themselves, no Super Glue or chassis needed
create.ponder.sail.text_3: Right-Click them with a Dye to colour them
create.ponder.sail.text_4: Right-Click them with Shears to strip them back down to frames
create.ponder.sail_frame.text_1: Sail Frames are a convenient way to build windmills
create.ponder.sail_frame.text_2: They stick to blocks and to each other by themselves, no Super Glue or chassis needed
create.ponder.mechanical_bearing.header: Moving Structures using the Mechanical Bearing
create.ponder.mechanical_bearing.text_1: A Mechanical Bearing latches on to the block in front of it
create.ponder.mechanical_bearing.text_2: When Rotational Force reaches it, it assembles that block and everything attached into a rotating contraption
create.ponder.bearing_modes.header: Movement Modes of the Mechanical Bearing
create.ponder.bearing_modes.text_1: When it stops, the bearing sets the structure down at the closest grid-aligned angle
create.ponder.bearing_modes.text_2: Its value panel can keep it from ever placing the blocks, or let it place them only close to the angle it started at
create.ponder.stabilized_bearings.text_1: When a Mechanical Bearing is itself part of a moving structure...
create.ponder.stabilized_bearings.text_2: ...it tries to keep itself standing upright
create.ponder.stabilized_bearings.text_3: Just like before, it attaches to the block in front of it
create.ponder.stabilized_bearings.text_4: As a result, the whole sub-contraption stays level while it travels
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_1: A Clockwork Bearing grips the blocks in front of it
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_2: Given Rotational Force, it turns the structure to match the current hour of the day
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_5: Right-Click the bearing to switch the animation on or off
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_6: A second structure can be put in front of the hour hand
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_7: Make sure the two structures are not glued together
create.ponder.clockwork_bearing.text_8: The second structure now turns as the minute hand
create.ponder.gantry_shaft.text_1: Gantry Shafts are the rail of a gantry: carriages mounted on them slide along them
create.ponder.gantry_shaft.text_2: A gantry can carry blocks that are attached to its carriage
create.ponder.gantry_carriage.text_1: Gantry Carriages clamp onto a Gantry Shaft and ride along it
create.ponder.gantry_carriage.text_2: A gantry can carry blocks that are attached to its carriage
create.ponder.gantry_redstone.text_1: Gantry Shafts powered by redstone stop moving their carriages
create.ponder.gantry_redstone.text_2: Instead, their Rotational Force is passed on to the carriage's output shaft
create.ponder.gantry_direction.text_1: Gantry Shafts can be placed facing either way along their axis
create.ponder.gantry_direction.text_2: Which way a carriage moves depends on the orientation of its shaft...
create.ponder.gantry_direction.text_3: ...and on the direction the shaft is turning
create.ponder.gantry_direction.text_4: The same rules decide which way the passed-on rotation turns
create.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_1: A Gantry Shaft attaches to a carriage without any Super Glue
create.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_2: The same goes for carriages riding on a shaft that is being moved
create.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_3: Chaining gantries like this lets one system move along several axes
create.ponder.cart_assembler.text_1: A powered Cart Assembler loads the structure resting on it onto a passing Minecart
create.ponder.cart_assembler.text_2: Without a signal it does the opposite: cart contraptions rolling over it are put back down as blocks
create.ponder.cart_assembler.text_3: Use a Wrench on the Minecart to pick up the whole contraption and take it elsewhere
create.ponder.cart_assembler_modes.text_: Cart contraptions turn to face the way their cart is moving
The arrow on the assembler shows which side of the structure counts as its front
Set the assembler to Lock Rotation, and the contraption keeps the same orientation no matter where it goes
create.ponder.cart_assembler_dual.text_1: When two Cart Assemblers carry one shared structure...
create.ponder.cart_assembler_dual.text_2: ...powering just one of them builds a Carriage Contraption
create.ponder.cart_assembler_dual.text_3: Its two carts then behave as if they were joined with a Minecart Coupling
create.ponder.cart_assembler_rails.heade: Other types of Minecarts and Rails
create.ponder.cart_assembler_rails.text_: On a plain rail, the Cart Assembler doesn't change how passing carts move
Placed on a Powered Rail, it holds the cart in place until it receives power
A Controller Rail under it behaves the same way: the cart waits for a signal
Minecarts with a Chest can serve as the anchor as well
create.ponder.mechanical_harvester.text_: When Mechanical Harvesters are carried along by a moving contraption...
...they reap every ripe crop they pass and replant it on the spot
create.ponder.mechanical_plough.text_1: When Mechanical Ploughs are carried along by a moving contraption...
create.ponder.mechanical_plough.text_2: ...they knock out any block that has no solid hitbox
create.ponder.mechanical_plough.text_3: They can also turn the ground below them into farmland
create.ponder.mechanical_plough.text_4: ...and fling entities in their path out of the way, without hurting them
create.ponder.contraption_controls.text_: Actors on a moving contraption are switched on by default
Contraption Controls let you turn them on and off while moving
They work wherever they are fixed on the contraption
While the contraption is disassembled, set its filter to target only one kind of actor
If it is powered by redstone when the contraption assembles...
...the actors it targets start out switched off
create.ponder.mechanical_roller_pave.hea: Clearing and Paving with the Roller
create.ponder.mechanical_roller_pave.tex: Mechanical Rollers tidy up the ground along tracks and paths
With no material set, its default mode just breaks the blocks in its way, much like a Drill
While the contraption is disassembled, you can give it a paving material
The material is drawn from chests or barrels mounted on the same structure
Now, besides clearing blocks away, it also lays a new surface underneath
Be aware that blocks a roller breaks may not drop anything
Rollers shine on Trains, but they work on most other moving contraptions too
create.ponder.mechanical_roller_fill.tex: While disassembled, rollers can be switched to other modes
The fill modes help close the gap between a raised path and the land below
In 'straight fill' they build plain columns down until they reach the ground
In 'sloped fill', each layer further down is placed a little wider
Unlike 'clear & pave', neither fill mode ever breaks blocks that are already there
create.ponder.redstone_contact.text_1: Two Redstone Contacts that face each other give off a redstone signal
create.ponder.redstone_contact.text_2: That still works when one of them is mounted on a moving contraption
